newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel to cut jobs at industrial fibre.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel to cut jobs at industrial fibre.

text.p: Dutch chemical group Akzo Nobel said on Wednesday it planned to shed several hundred jobs at its industrial fibres unit over the next three years.

"Several hundred jobs of a total 5,300 will go, that is quite normal within the context of the ongoing rationalisation in the industry," Akzo Nobel spokesman Huub Verbeeten said, commenting on trade journal reports.
Akzo's industrial fibres production in Europe is concentrated at Emmen in the northern Netherlands and a larger site at Obernburg in Germany, which employs 3,800.

Folkert Blaisse, general manager of Akzo Nobel's industrial fibres business unit, told trade journal European Chemical News in an interview this week his short term goal was to boost profitability through internal growth and "with a drastic improvement in the cost structure".

Industrial fibres account for around 44 percent of sales at Akzo Nobel's fibres division, which posted nine-month operating profits of 2.59 billion guilders in 1996, down from 2.73 billion a year earlier.
